title: Thus Saith the Mercy of the Lord
description: Thus Saith the Mercy of the Lord in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 121, headed “Children devoted to God, Gen. 17. 7 10. Acts 16. 14 15 33. (For those who practise infant Baptism.)”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thus saith the mer-cy of the Lord, "I'll be a God to thee; "I'll bless thy nu-merous race, and they "Shall be a seed for me."

lines: Thus saith the mercy of the Lord,
"I'll bless thy numerous race, and they
And gave his sons to God;
But water seals the blessing now,
That once was seal'd with blood.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
